identity.title: Star Formation Efficiency per Free-fall Time in nearby Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using new, high resolution CO imaging from the PHANGS-ALMA survey, we estimate the gravitational free-fall time at 60 to 120 pc resolution

evidence.quote: We estimate molecular gas surface density from PHANGS-ALMA CO (2–1) data for $11$ targets and archival CO data for M31 (cite: CALDUPRIMO16), M33 (cite: DRUARD14), and M51 (cite: SCHINNER13).

question.value: What is the star formation efficiency per free-fall time (eps_ff) in nearby galaxies, from GMC-scale CO maps combined with molecular gas depletion times?

evidence.quote: we estimate the gravitational free-fall time at 60 to 120 pc resolution, and contrast this with the local molecular gas depletion time to estimate $\epsilon_{\rm ff}$.
PHANGS-ALMA CO (2–1) data for $11$ targets
PHANGS-ALMA uses ALMA’s 12m, 7m, and total power antennas to map CO (2–1) emission
at native angular resolution of $1-1.5\ensuremath{''}$. This translates to native physical resolutions of $\sim~60{-}120$ pc

max_recoverable_scale.value: sensitive to all spatial scales (ACA + total power)

evidence.quote: we expect these maps to be sensitive to emission at all spatial scales.
the CO data cubes have rms noise of $\sim0.1$ K per $2.5$ km s$^{-1}$ channel.
The WISE maps are derived from the unWISE reprocessing of (cite: LANG14).

analysis_steps.goal: CO to molecular gas surface density

method.value: Convert CO integrated intensity with fixed alpha_CO and inclination correction

evidence.quote: We adopt a fixed CO(2–1)-to-H$_2$ conversion factor $\alpha_{\rm CO}^{2-1} = 6.2$ M$_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$ (K km s$^{-1}$)$^{-1}$.

key_parameters.value: alpha_CO(2-1)=6.2; alpha_CO(1-0)=4.35 for M31 and M51

evidence.quote: For those we use $\alpha_{\rm CO}^{1-0} = 4.35$ M$_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$ (K km s$^{-1}$)$^{-1}$ with no line ratio term.
with a typical CO(2–1)/CO(1–0) line ratio of 0.7
We explore the effect of a metallicity-dependent $\alpha_{\rm CO}$ on our results for these cases.

analysis_steps.goal: SFR surface density and depletion time at 1.3 kpc

method.value: Sigma_SFR = K I_nu with FUV+22um benchmark; tau_dep = Sigma_mol/Sigma_SFR at 1.3 kpc

evidence.quote: We use hybrid tracers by adding the SFR derived from each choice of UV and IR band, and adopt SFR(FUV+22$\mu$m) as a benchmark.
$K=1.04 \times 10^{-1}$, $1.04 \times 10^{-1}$, $3.77 \times 10^{-3}$, and $2.97 \times 10^{-3}$ for FUV, NUV, 12$\mu$m, and 24$\mu$m bands, respectively
we test the effect of using NUV instead of FUV and using 12$\mu$m instead of 22$\mu$m.

method.value: tau_ff = sqrt(3 pi H /(32 G Sigma_mol)) with rho = Sigma_mol/H

evidence.quote: we combine our measured, high physical resolutions ($60{-}120$ pc) $\Sigma_{\rm mol}$ with an estimate of the line-of-sight depth through the molecular gas layer, $H$

key_parameters.value: Default H = 100 pc; alternatives hydrostatic (h*=300 pc, M/L=0.5; median H 122 pc) and virial cloud (alpha_vir~2; median H 116 pc)

evidence.loc: 3.3 Thickness of the Molecular Gas Layer
evidence.quote: *Fixed $H=100$ pc.* This is roughly the diameter of a large molecular cloud

validation.value: Compare eps_ff across three H prescriptions

evidence.loc: 3.3 Thickness of the Molecular Gas Layer
evidence.quote: We calculate $H$ using each method above and compare the resulting $\epsilon_{\rm ff}$ to estimate the systematic uncertainty associated with estimating $H$.

method.value: Mass-weighted mean of tau_ff^-1 within each 1.3 kpc beam via convolution

evidence.quote: we calculate the mass-weighted average of $\tau_{\rm ff}$ within each $1.3$ kpc region of a galaxy.
Hereby, we assume that $\left<\tau_{\rm ff, 60 pc}\right>_{\rm 1.3 kpc}^{-1} \approx \left<\tau_{\rm ff, 60 pc}^{-1}\right>_{\rm 1.3 kpc}$.

validation.value: Differs from Leroy17 approach by ~7% in tau_ff

evidence.quote: with the mean $\left<\mbox{$\tau_{\rm ff}$}_{\rm ,60pc}\right>_{\rm 1.3 kpc}$ differing by only $\sim 7\%$.

method.value: Monte Carlo of lognormal Sigma_mol distribution gives f_C(C); eps_ff = <tau_ff>/tau_dep

evidence.quote: We randomly draw $10^6$ samples from a lognormal distribution designed to simulate the true distribution of mass as a function of $\Sigma_{\rm mol}$
These model distributions have $1\sigma$ width of $0.5$ dex.

validation.value: Systematics explored by varying SFR tracer, H, completeness, alpha_CO, resolution

evidence.quote: where we vary our adopted SFR tracer, the line-of-sight depth, completeness correction, the CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor, and linear resolution.
we find median $\mbox{$\epsilon_{\rm ff}$}\approx 0.7\%$ across all lines-of-sight in $14$ galaxies

claims.finding: eps_ff anti-correlates with stellar mass, partly explained by metallicity-dependent alpha_CO

evidence.quote: even with this metallicity correction, there is still a significant anti-correlation between galaxy stellar mass and $\epsilon_{\rm ff}$

evidence.quote: These observations recover the surface density of molecular gas at high physical resolution, which is closely related to the mean volume density.
